scenes.title: Mauritanie, N'Titane (Adrar)
scenes.description: A press photograph from Agence Rol, taken in 1908, showing N'Titane in Adrar. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie.
scenes.explanation: Clear polyethylene terephthalate bottles did not exist in 1908, so no one in the scene could have owned or discarded one.

source.description: Référence bibliographique : Rol, 2492 Appartient à l’ensemble documentaire : Pho20Rol

scenes.title: Trondheim. Kongens gate
scenes.description: A photograph from the National Library of Norway shows Kongens gate in Trondheim in 1949. The record does not name the photographer.
scenes.explanation: The lightweight folding kick scooter with small wheels and a metal deck did not exist in 1949.
scenes.credit: Mittet & Co. AS via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: 25/6/27, Spad Lorraine du lieutenant Challe [avion]
scenes.description: A press photograph from Agence Rol dated 25 June 1927 shows the Spad Lorraine aircraft of Lieutenant Challe. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, EI-13 (153).
scenes.explanation: The one-piece nylon cable tie was patented in 1958, so no such strap could exist on an aircraft photographed in 1927.

scenes.title: [Canon dans une tranchée]
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol showing a cannon in a trench, dated April 1917. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, and relates to the Guerre de tranchées.
scenes.explanation: Solar-powered LED garden lights did not exist in 1917; they only became common consumer products in the 1990s.

scenes.title: Ligne de Pau à Oloron. Pont de Pau - Novembre
scenes.description: A photograph from November 1880 shows the Pont de Pau on the railway line from Pau to Oloron, held by the Ecole nationale des ponts et chaussées (PH 272 P.2) and in the public domain via the Bibliothèque nationale de France. The record does not name a photographer.
scenes.explanation: The tower crane was not invented until the mid-20th century, so it cannot exist in an 1880 construction scene.
